overall_summary: Bitcoin is caught between clear selling pressure and steady institutional demand. Heavy spot ETF outflows and fresh exchange-hack headlines are weighing on sentiment, while Strategy buys and Tether’s large disclosed holdings provide a strong offset. Macro is mixed with softer yields and oil, but unresolved geopolitics and data keep the tone cautious rather than directional.
key_points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs bleed $399M in outflows
Strategy adds BTC; Tether holds 150k coins
Hacks hit Binance SAFU and Mercado Bitcoin
Yields ease and oil drops on diplomacy hopes
Iran strikes and Ukraine fighting keep risk premium

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $399M; IBIT Sees Biggest Outflow Since June
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about three hundred ninety-nine million dollars in net outflows on Monday, with BlackRock's IBIT alone seeing over four hundred five million dollars leave—its largest single-day redemption since June. That follows a six-hundred-forty-three million dollar outflow the prior session, leaving Bitcoin dipping toward seventy-six thousand three hundred as it eyes a fifth straight weekly loss. Traders should care because sustained ETF selling removes a key institutional bid right as midterm election uncertainty and tech weakness add pressure. Watch whether flows stabilize after the vote or keep draining support.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure near key support; risks deeper test of 76k if outflows continue

items.title: Binance SAFU Fund Halved After Hack; North Korea Denies Role
items.summary: On-chain data shows Binance spent roughly half its SAFU Bitcoin—about seven thousand five hundred BTC or five hundred eighty million dollars—to help cover the six-point-three billion dollar hack, dropping the fund below its own eight hundred million dollar top-up threshold with no refill timeline announced. North Korea's Kim Yo Jong called FBI attribution to TraderTraitor absurd political provocation, while Binance says outflows have normalized, it has replenished about ninety-five percent of stolen assets, and remains in strong financial health. This keeps confidence fragile for the largest exchange and the broader market still digesting the largest crypto heist ever. Traders need to monitor any further user withdrawals or proof-of-reserves updates.
items.impact: Ongoing confidence drag and potential residual outflows; thinner insurance buffer raises risk premium

items.title: Tether CEO Reveals 150,000 Bitcoin Holdings Worth $11.5 Billion
items.summary: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said at the Plan B Forum the company holds give or take one hundred fifty thousand bitcoin, valued at roughly eleven point five billion dollars—about fifty thousand more than implied by its latest USDT reserve attestation. The extra coins sit outside the stablecoin reserves, likely in corporate investments, and he did not detail acquisition timing. This cements Tether as one of the largest known corporate Bitcoin holders behind only Strategy. For traders it signals continued large-scale accumulation by a major stablecoin issuer that can lock up supply, though transparency on the non-reserve stack remains limited.
items.impact: Positive supply-side signal from major holder; supports longer-term accumulation narrative

items.title: Liquid Network Fully Restores 1:1 Bitcoin Backing After Exploit
items.summary: The Liquid Federation announced bitcoin reserves are fully restored, reestablishing one-to-one backing for all LBTC nearly two months after a September software bug allowed roughly four thousand unbacked tokens to be redeemed for real bitcoin. A final two hundred fifty BTC transfer closed the remaining gap after the attacker returned most funds; the source of the make-up capital was not disclosed. Swaps have been running at one-to-one via providers, while direct peg-outs stay under enhanced controls. This removes an overhang for a key Bitcoin sidechain used by exchanges and traders and restores verifiable reserves.
items.impact: Restores confidence in Liquid infrastructure; minor positive for Bitcoin ecosystem liquidity tools

items.title: Mercado Bitcoin Hacked for ~$40M; Exchange Pledges Full User Coverage
items.summary: Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin confirmed a security incident that drained hot wallets across at least ten blockchains, with estimates around thirty-eight to forty-eight million dollars. The firm suspended deposits and withdrawals, said no customer data leaked, and pledged to cover all user losses from its own funds while partners including Tether froze roughly eleven million. The attack comes days after the Binance heist and adds to a wave of exchange security incidents. Traders should note the coverage promise limits immediate contagion but highlights ongoing hot-wallet risks across the industry.
items.impact: Limited direct BTC price impact if fully covered; reinforces exchange-risk caution

items.title: Strategy Adds 811 Bitcoin, Lifting Holdings to 849,327 BTC
items.summary: Strategy disclosed it bought eight hundred eleven bitcoin for sixty-five point five million dollars last week at an average of about eighty thousand eight hundred forty-six dollars, bringing total holdings to eight hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred twenty-seven BTC. The purchase was funded via at-the-market stock sales and came after a brief pause, alongside a larger preferred-share repurchase. Michael Saylor continues the treasury accumulation strategy even as price sits well below recent highs. This remains one of the steadiest institutional bids in the market and shows corporate buyers still stepping in on dips.
items.impact: Steady corporate demand absorbs some supply; supports floor narrative amid ETF selling

items.title: Oil Plunges Over 7% on Iran Diplomacy Hopes
items.summary: Brent crude dropped about seven point six percent to settle near one hundred four seventy-seven dollars a barrel, while WTI fell roughly seven point four percent to about ninety-six forty-six. The move came after signals from Tehran and Washington that peace talks could ease Middle East supply risks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Traders should care because cheaper energy cools inflation expectations, eases pressure on bond yields, and can support risk assets including Bitcoin if the relief holds.
items.impact: Disinflationary relief that could lower rate-hike odds and lift risk appetite

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Jumps to 55.5 in October
items.summary: The Institute for Supply Management factory index rose one point to fifty-five point five, beating forecasts around fifty-four point six and marking a tenth straight month of expansion. Production hit its highest since late twenty twenty-one at fifty-nine, while the prices-paid index eased to seventy-five point two from seventy-seven point nine. Crypto traders watch this because solid growth keeps the Fed data-dependent and December hike odds alive, even as softer input prices offer a mild disinflationary offset.
items.impact: Growth strength supports hawkish Fed pricing; cooler prices limit the upside for yields

items.title: RBA Hikes Cash Rate to 4.85 Percent in Split Vote
items.summary: Australia’s Reserve Bank raised its cash rate twenty-five basis points to four point eight five percent, the highest since two thousand eight and its fifth hike this year. The six-to-three vote dropped explicit language about further tightening and left markets pricing a likely pause next. Global traders care because another major central bank is still fighting energy-driven inflation, which keeps global liquidity tighter and can weigh on risk assets until growth softens.
items.impact: Tighter global financial conditions and higher Australian yields pressure risk sentiment

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Eases Near 4.9 Percent; DXY Steady
items.summary: The ten-year Treasury yield slipped toward four point nine percent after oil’s plunge and mixed data, down from recent highs above five percent. The dollar index held around one hundred one point seven to one hundred one point eight. For Bitcoin traders this matters because lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets and can ease financial conditions if the move sticks ahead of Friday’s jobs report.
items.impact: Softer yields and stable dollar support risk assets if disinflation narrative holds

items.title: JOLTS Job Openings Report Due Today at 10 AM ET
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases September JOLTS this morning, with openings expected near seven point one million after August’s seven point zero seven nine million. Hires, quits and layoffs will give the first major labor read before Friday’s nonfarm payrolls. Crypto markets watch labor data closely because cooler openings could pull rate expectations lower, while resilient demand would keep December Fed hike odds elevated.
items.impact: Key labor catalyst that can swing rate-path pricing ahead of NFP

items.title: Construction Spending Falls 1.9 Percent in September
items.summary: Census Bureau data showed total construction outlays dropped one point nine percent to an annualized two point one eight six trillion dollars, missing expectations of a gain and driven by a five point five percent plunge in private residential spending. Nonresidential held up better, helped by data-center and power projects. Soft housing-related spending is a mild growth drag that could lean against higher-for-longer rate bets if it continues.
items.impact: Soft residential data adds modest dovish lean to the growth picture

items.title: US Midterms Underway as Referendum on Trump
items.summary: Americans are voting today in midterm elections that will decide control of the House and Senate. Polls and prediction markets give Democrats strong odds of taking both chambers, driven by voter anger over high prices and the unpopular Iran war. A split or Democratic Congress would mean gridlock and more investigations for the rest of Trump's term. Traders should watch for policy uncertainty on spending, taxes, regulation, and foreign policy that could swing risk assets once results clarify.
items.impact: Elevated volatility and policy uncertainty until results firm

items.title: US Hits Iran Qeshm Island in Limited Defensive Strikes
items.summary: US forces struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Monday in what officials called a defensive response to Iranian surface-to-air missiles and fire at US assets. The action was limited and not a full resumption of major combat, coming even as Trump and Vance talk up possible deals and Iran signals openness to talks via Qatari mediators. Explosions were reported by Iranian media. This keeps Hormuz risk alive for oil and shipping right as midterms unfold, so risk assets face mixed war-or-diplomacy headlines.
items.impact: Geopolitical risk premium and energy volatility rebound

items.title: Oil Plunges Then Steadies on Iran Talk Hopes and Strikes
items.summary: Brent crude crashed more than seven percent on Monday to around one hundred five dollars on signals that Iran's supreme leader greenlit talks and Trump said a deal could happen, easing supply fears after months of Hormuz disruption. Prices steadied or edged higher Tuesday after the Qeshm strikes news. European gas also tumbled hard. Lower oil helps inflation and risk appetite, but the strike reminder shows the war premium can snap back fast. Crypto traders care because energy shocks still drive broader risk-on or risk-off moves.
items.impact: Lower oil supportive if talks stick; strikes reverse gains

items.title: Russia Bombs Ukraine Aid Site, Toll Hits 30-Plus
items.summary: A Russian guided-bomb attack on a school used as a humanitarian aid point and nearby shelter in Zaporizhzhia killed at least twenty-six to thirty-one people, with dozens still missing. Zelensky called it proof Russia wants no de-escalation. Overnight Russia also launched hundreds of drones and missiles across multiple regions, hitting power and hospitals, timed with US election day. The strike follows the end of a short local ceasefire. This keeps the Ukraine war hot and energy/grain risks elevated for global markets.
items.impact: Renewed escalation risk and pressure on European energy

items.title: Russia, Ukraine, US Set Abu Dhabi Peace Talks
items.summary: The Kremlin confirmed trilateral working-level peace talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi on November tenth and eleventh. US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to lead for Washington; Russia's Medinsky for Moscow. Topics include post-war security, de-escalation, and humanitarian steps. This comes right after the deadly aid strike and a brief local truce. Any real progress would ease a major long-running risk, but gaps remain wide so markets will treat it as a watch item rather than a done deal.
items.impact: Potential de-escalation catalyst if talks advance

items.title: US Ends AGOA Benefits for South Africa, Rwanda
items.summary: The Trump administration notified Congress it will terminate South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act duty-free trade program starting January first twenty twenty-seven. Officials cited trade barriers, corruption, human rights, rule-of-law issues, and threats to US interests. South Africa is the biggest AGOA user with about one point seven billion in exports including cars, wine, and citrus. This escalates bilateral friction and fits a broader protectionist tilt that markets watch for spillover into other trade disputes.
items.impact: Signals tougher US trade stance, mild emerging-market pressure
